title: The conjecture on unicentroidal trees with edge-reconstruction number 3
statement:
Let $\text{ern}(G)$ denote the edge-reconstruction number of a graph $G$, namely the minimum number of edge-deleted subgraphs $G-e$ sufficient to determine $G$ up to isomorphism. A tree is **unicentroidal** if it has a single centroid.

**The unicentroidal edge-reconstruction conjecture.** The only infinite classes of unicentroidal trees which have $\text{ern}=3$ are the paths on an odd number of vertices, the caterpillars $C(2,0,\ldots,0,2)$ of even diameter, and the family of trees $T_k$ depicted in Figure.

The paper reports these three infinite families from computer searches and conjectures that no other infinite families of unicentroidal trees have edge-reconstruction number 3. The surrounding results establish the corresponding classification for bicentroidal trees apart from three stated exceptions; the conjecture concerns the remaining unicentroidal case.
source_name: Kevin Asciak, Josef Lauri, Wendy Myrvold and Virgilio Pannone, “On the edge-reconstruction number of a tree”, arXiv:1312.1234 (2013).
